subject: Energy
title: What Is Energy Justice?
description: A short lesson to help you apply What Is Energy Justice?.

hook.text: Energy justice asks who benefits from energy systems and who bears the burdens—pollution, cost, and displacement.

buildup.text: Fossil fuel infrastructure is often sited near low-income and minority communities—exposing them to the worst pollution.

discovery.text: Three pillars: distributional (who gets what), procedural (who decides), and recognition (whose voice is heard).

twist.text: The clean energy transition could repeat old injustices—if solar and storage benefits flow only to wealthy homeowners.

climax.text: Community solar programs let renters and low-income households access clean energy—broadening who benefits.

punchline.text: Clean energy for all, not just the affluent—that's energy justice.

quiz.question: What are the three pillars of energy justice?
